title: Lorraine Massimino’s Meatballs and Sunday Sauce
source: From Lorraine Massimino  ·  Family dinners and gatherings
headnote: A recipe from Karen’s mom, Lorraine Massimino, inspired by her husband Tom’s Italian roots: beef and pork meatballs browned and then simmered slowly in a big pot of Sunday sauce.

items.raw: 1 cup fresh breadcrumbs (from 2 slices crustless bread)
½ cup grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan
2 teaspoons kosher salt and ½ teaspoon black pepper
1 large onion, finely chopped, and 4 garlic cloves, minced
1 cup water or dry red wine
1 bay leaf, ½ teaspoon dried oregano, a few basil leaves

steps.text: Mash the breadcrumbs and milk together in a large bowl and let them sit 5 minutes. This paste is what keeps the meatballs tender.
Add the beef, pork, eggs, cheese, garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix with your hands just until evenly combined — overworking makes them tough.
Roll into 1½- to 2-inch balls with wet hands and set on a tray. You should have about 24.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a wide heavy pot over medium-high. Brown the meatballs in batches on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes per batch. They will finish cooking in the sauce.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat. Cook the onion over medium heat 6 to 8 minutes until soft, add the garlic for 1 minute, then stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until it darkens.

Add the crushed tomatoes, water or wine, bay leaf, oregano, and basil, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a simmer, return the meatballs, and cook partly covered on low for 1½ to 2 hours, stirring gently now and then.
Remove the bay leaf, taste for salt, and serve over pasta with more grated cheese.

notes.label: Taste the mix
notes.text: fry a teaspoon of the meat mixture before rolling them all, and adjust the salt.

notes.label: Freezing
notes.text: cool completely and freeze meatballs in their sauce up to 3 months. Thaw overnight and reheat gently on the stove.

notes.label: Other meats
notes.text: all beef, or a third each beef, pork, and veal. Sausage or braciole can simmer in the same pot.

notes.label: Make a big batch
notes.text: the recipe doubles easily in a large Dutch oven.

openQuestion: Anything that is Lorraine’s own here — the bread or breadcrumbs, the cheese, wine or water in the sauce, other meats in the pot? And who carries it on now?
